clue.text: Bum mix of Cure song

indicators.note: a mix of something is its parts jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling remix of a track by the Cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is a verb here, as in to bum a cigarette, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to cadge or beg something from someone without paying for it.

clue.text: First 6 of 10 could become greatest in years

indicators.note: the letters could become a different word when rearranged
only the opening six letters of that word are kept, so its last two are dropped

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, guiding star

explanation.surface: A puzzle cross-reference musing on what a word might turn into.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the first six letters of LODESTAR leaves LODEST, which 'could become' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest person in a group is the one with the greatest age, the most years lived.

clue.text: Sound of person dying inside container of poisonous gases

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
the outside letters of the word form a container around the other piece

parts.note: a death rattle is the noise in the throat of someone dying

explanation.surface: A grim scene of someone expiring in a tank of toxic gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gases' looks like part of the scene but is the definition, a verb: chatters. 'container of' takes P and S, the outside of 'poisonous'; 'inside' puts RATTLE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas, informally, is to talk idly at length, which is what someone who prattles does.

clue.text: Time to take heart from award

indicators.note: removing the heart means the central letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: an honour is an award such as a knighthood

explanation.surface: A suggestion that it is time to draw encouragement from a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take heart from' looks like 'be encouraged by' but removes the middle letters N and O of HONOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes long.

clue.text: Listed building is least occupied

indicators.note: building is read as constructing, so the letters are assembled into a new word

explanation.surface: A protected heritage building that stands mostly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed building' is a British term for a protected historic building; here 'building' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is idle has nothing to do, so the most idle is the least busy.

clue.text: Cold beer produced strange thoughts here

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: produced means made into something new, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Chilled beer gave someone peculiar ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges BEER into EREB.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the main part of the brain, where conscious thinking takes place.

clue.text: Nirvana cover recorded in urinal oddly

indicators.note: something recorded in a book is written within it, so one piece goes inside the other
oddly means the letters in odd positions of the word are kept

parts.note: a top is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: A cover version of a Nirvana song captured in a gents' toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana looks like the grunge band but is a state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both denote an ideal state of perfect happiness, paradise.

clue.text: False religion briefly embroiled in row about vision

indicators.note: embroiled in means caught up inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to row a boat uses an oar

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a cult is a sect often regarded as a false religion

explanation.surface: A sham religion caught up in a dispute over a prophetic vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface but is the boating sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eyes and sight.

clue.text: Snippets from books by author delving into probability

indicators.note: delving into means digging inside, so pieces go within another

parts.note: odds express the probability of something
the author of a clue may call themselves me
NT is the New Testament, a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Extracts from literature by a writer researching chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover scraps or fragments, small bits of something.

clue.text: Guide expected work reported by headline

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: a load, as in workload, is the amount of work expected of someone
to headline a show is to star in it

explanation.surface: A manual of anticipated tasks, as covered under a newspaper headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used for navigation, so figuratively a guiding principle.

clue.text: Having no duties former employee casually taking time to finish

indicators.note: taking means the first pieces take on another one
to finish means the extra piece goes at the very end

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
emp is an informal shortening of employee

explanation.surface: A former member of staff with nothing to do, idly taking their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means freed from an obligation such as tax or service.

clue.text: Gradually introduce detailed steps to follow at home

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence

explanation.surface: Instructions for a detailed home routine to be learned step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but is read as de-tailed, losing its last letter; 'to follow' puts that piece second.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea or habit is to put it into someone's mind slowly over time.

clue.text: Drivers start to turn in space when reversing vehicle

indicators.note: reversing means the whole assembled string is read backwards

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: one piece is put in another

parts.note: room means space

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Motorists beginning a turn in a parking space while backing up their car.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into ROOM to make ROTOM; RAC plus ROTOM, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor car is an automobile, a road vehicle.

clue.text: Old lady gets cross over gnome

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old lady

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a cross is a mix, a hybrid of two breeds

explanation.surface: A mother annoyed with a garden ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' is not the garden figure but its rarer sense: a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in the sense of an aphorism is a short wise saying, a proverb.

clue.text: Horse throws popular champion

indicators.note: throws means casts off, so a part is removed

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A racehorse unseats its favourite jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is drug slang, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of a cause is someone admired for defending it, a figure looked up to.

clue.text: Cost of excursion, including travel

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: The price of a day trip, with transport thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost' is a noun; the answer is the British noun for an expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are expenses, money spent.

clue.text: Poles on Greek Island confused German

indicators.note: points the solver to the letters N and S, the compass poles, at the word's ends
confused means mixed up, so letters change places

parts.note: Naxos is an island in the Greek Cyclades

explanation.surface: Polish tourists on a Greek island bewildered by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but N and S; 'confused' swaps those two letters at the ends of NAXOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxons were a Germanic people, and Saxony is a German state.

clue.text: Deadly agent in The New Avengers

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lethal spy in the 1970s British TV series The New Avengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The New Avengers' reads as a title, but 'New' signals an anagram of AVENGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a lethal chemical weapon, an agent that attacks the nervous system.

clue.text: Eminence of name-dropping intellectuals

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Mensa is a society for people with a high IQ

explanation.surface: The prominence enjoyed by brainy types who boast about famous friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' means a height of land, not distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a piece of high ground; a mesa is a flat-topped hill.

clue.text: Limited coverage was initially breaking SIM cards of similar design

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so a letter goes inside
initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: a suit is a set of playing cards marked with the same symbol

explanation.surface: A news report on a phone network with patchy signal and lookalike SIM cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit covers only part of the body, so it gives limited coverage.

clue.text: Case in point symbolises this valuable material

definitions.text: Case in point symbolises this valuable material

parts.words: Case in point symbolises this valuable material
parts.note: the case, the outer letters, of point are P and T, the chemical symbol of this precious metal

explanation.surface: A typical example stands for something precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case in point' looks like 'example' but means the outer letters of 'point', PT, the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This precious metal is valued in jewellery and industry and has the symbol Pt.

clue.text: Fruit found in illuminated character of Greek text

parts.note: lit means illuminated
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A fruit discovered in the decorated letter of a Greek manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illuminated' suggests a decorated manuscript but simply means lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, usually spelt lychee, is a small sweet Chinese fruit.

clue.text: Engraving that is inspired by last of Jackson Pollock's three pivotal pieces

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so one piece is taken inside the other
the last letter of the word is taken
the three central letters of the name are taken

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An engraving influenced by Jackson Pollock's key works.
explanation.walkthrough: N (end of Jackson) and LLO (middle three of Pollock) take in IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to fill incised designs, and an item decorated that way.

clue.text: Regret loyal friend announced instructions to candidates

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word sounds like the pieces

parts.note: to rue is to regret; a brick is British slang for a reliable, loyal friend

explanation.surface: Remorse at a faithful companion's public statement of exam directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of directions heading an exam paper.

clue.text: You are caught entering young man's office

indicators.note: entering means going in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a beau is a young man, a boyfriend

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the sound of the words gives the letters

parts.note: said aloud, the two words you are sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: You're found sneaking into a young man's workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like 'trapped' but means heard: 'you are' heard is U R.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency, as in a travel bureau.

clue.text: Extracting power from unstable isotope is superfluous

indicators.note: unstable means liable to change, so the remaining letters are rearranged
extracting means pulling out, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A physics lab note that removing energy from a radioactive isotope is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from ISOTOPE leaves ISOTOE, rearranged by 'unstable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no useful purpose, so redundant.

clue.text: Electra's complex is most understandable

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that the Electra complex is the easiest psychological theory to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electra's complex' is the Freudian term, but 'complex' signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearest is the superlative of clear, meaning easy to grasp.

clue.text: Heartless scoundrel regularly failing to turn up

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word goes
every other letter of what remains fails, dropping out at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A rogue without compassion who keeps not showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless SCOUNDREL is SCOUDREL; dropping its odd letters leaves the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl is to bend or roll upwards, as a lip or leaf does.

clue.text: "Friend" wants name included in credit

indicators.note: included in means placed within another piece

parts.note: a handle is a slang word for a name

explanation.surface: A pal wants their name listed among the end credits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' in quotes points to the sitcom Friends, whose character Chandler Bing is one of the friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandler Bing is one of the six title characters of the US sitcom Friends.

clue.text: Inability to coordinate drivers locking vehicle

indicators.note: locking means holding in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation
a taxi is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Motorists unable to work together to lock a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is a medical loss of control over bodily movements.
